newsitem.title: USA: Clinton softens opposition to budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Clinton softens opposition to budget amendment.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday softened his opposition to a constitutional amendment requiring a balanced budget, saying he could live with one if it was flexible enough to permit anti-recession moves.
"I just want to make sure that if we have one ... it needs to clearly give us the possibility of dealing with a recession," Clinton told reporters after signing parks legislation at the White House.

Clinton seemed to be bowing to last week's congressional election results, which made the passage of a balanced budget ammendment almost inevitable. Republicans made a net gain of two seats in the U.S. Senate, where the budget plan failed by one vote in the last Congress.
"My problems with a constitutional ammendment were always more a question of how to manage the larger economic problems of the country," Clinton said.

"We don't want to wind up in a Congress some day or (in) a recession raising taxes or throwing unemployed people off health care because we're trying to reach a balanced budget," he added. "You could actually wind up making the deficit worse."

"If it sets a framework that says that in the 21st Century in the economy that we're going to be living in, other things being equal, we ought always to be balancing our books, I agree with that," Clinmton said, adding his concern was that "we may tie our hands more than we will achieve."
